title: Protect streaming clients from mid-response truncation with per-tenant circuit-breaker and backfill
creator: Aisha Cole
description: Multiple customers reported mid-response truncation and silent disconnects from the Hosted streaming API (SSE). Symptoms: final tokens missing, clients receive EOF without final chunk, SDKs report OK but result incomplete. Incidents spike correlated with gateway CPU pressure and GC pauses on routing nodes. This ticket implements a per-tenant streaming circuit-breaker at the gateway layer and an asynchronous backfill service that repairs partial outputs by replaying the final segment via a non-streaming path. Goal: prevent noisy partial outputs from reaching customers and provide automated backfill for any truncated sessions within a 24-hour window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use hosted streaming endpoint with long-response generation (>2048 tokens) and simulated gateway CPU load (stress-ng or p95 clients).
2) Introduce a short pause on an upstream routing node (GC or SIGSTOP) during generation to trigger mid-response truncation,
3) Observe client SSE stream ends without final 'done' event and last token boundary incomplete,
4) Reproduce with SDKs (node/react-native/python) to capture client-visible behavior and verify that reconnect does not produce deterministic finalization without replay.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: telemetry shows a class of sessions closed by gateway with 200 but missing finalChunk marker; edge proxies delivered 'connection reset' while backend considered request in-flight.
Correlation found between spike in gateway CPU/memory pressure and truncated streams; routing process sometimes closed sockets during transient OOM/eviction windows.
KV-cache and batching state is intact in model containers; truncated output is not a model fault but a transport finalization problem at the gateway layer.
Customer-reported examples (redacted) included timestamps and request-ids: r-8f7d, r-9c1a showing truncation at token offsets 1789-1802.
proposed_solution: A) Add per-tenant streaming circuit-breaker in gateway: maintain a short health score and when degraded, fail streaming handshake with explicit 503 + Retry-After instead of allowing partial output to flow. This prevents clients from receiving incomplete final outputs.

B) Implement an on-demand backfill worker: when gateway detects an abrupt closure of a streaming session and the request is eligible (non-sensitive data policy), enqueue a backfill job that replays the final segment using a non-streaming, idempotent generation call and attaches a backfill artifact to the session record.
C) SDK update: expose a 'streamFinalizationHint' flag in client SDKs so clients can accept asynchronous backfill notifications and merge results into the UI when available.
D) Telemetry: emit 'stream_truncated' and 'backfill_enqueued' events with request_id, tenant_id, and last_token_index to enable downstream analytics and customer reporting.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gateway rejects new streaming sessions for tenants marked degraded and returns deterministic 503 with Retry-After, instead of allowing partial streams to be delivered.
2) For truncated sessions, backfill jobs are queued and run reliably; backfill results are attached to session record and retrievable via the Admin API.
3) SDKs can opt into backfill notifications and correctly merge asynchronous final segments for at least node and python SDKs.
4) End-to-end tests simulate gateway pressure and verify no customer-visible truncated responses escape without either immediate 503 or a follow-up backfill within SLAs (24h).
5) Dashboard shows reduced customer escalations for truncation-class incidents in the following 30 days.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy circuit-breaker gating in canary region for 10% of tenants for 48h. Monitor stream_truncated, success_rate, and false-positive rejections.
Phase 2 (region ramp): Expand to 50%+ tenants and enable backfill worker in passive mode (dry-run) to validate reconstruction fidelity.
Phase 3 (active): Turn on backfill for non-sensitive sessions; release SDK patch simultaneously and notify customers in the status page.
Phase 4 (post-rollout): Keep circuit-breaker telemetry and backfill metrics in Console dashboard and run weekly audit for missed backfills.
testing_plan: Unit tests for circuit-breaker logic and tenant score decay,
Integration test injecting connection resets and verifying backfill enqueue and result attachment,
Chaos test: run premature gateway process restart during generation and assert behavior per acceptance criteria,
SDK compatibility tests across Node/Python/Rust clients for backfill hooks.
risks_and_mitigation: False positives: circuit-breaker might block streams unnecessarily. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and automatic cooldown with exponential backoff,
Backfill consistency: regenerated final segment must match original semantics. Mitigation: use same model version + deterministic seeds when available and attach provenance metadata to backfill,
Data sensitivity: replaying content may be disallowed for some tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant opt-out flag and respect privacy labels.
notes: Customer comms: sent targeted incident summary to affected customers on 2025-02-14; offered dedicated support and temporary routing exemptions while canary was live.
Support runbook updated with steps to manually trigger backfill and to set tenant backfill opt-out,
SRE: allocated two on-call engineers for the first 72h of rollout to handle escalations and revert if false-positive rejection rate >2%.
